_doc: Per-GPU-type pay targets in USD per card-hour (vault 23 section 7a). USD is the target; alpha is what is paid: each window the ledger converts these to alpha weights at the oracle price, holds the last good price if the oracle fails, and splits the serving emission across cards by accrued weight. Below target_fleet the unspent remainder recycles; above it per-card pay dilutes. idle: while IDLE and proof-passing. leased: while LEASED and healthy (the four pay conditions). STARTING, DRAINING, CHECKING earn nothing. Set by hand; the leased/idle ratio must stay above 1. 5090: Kimbo 2026-09-14. The six types added 2026-10-05 take their leased rate from the midpoint of the published on-demand rental prices in the 10/5 pricing sheet (Runpod, Lambda, DigitalOcean) and idle at 35% of leased, the 5090's own ratio; H100 is the exception: the sheet's $2.89-4.41 is far above what Lium pays an idle H100 ($1.49/h anchor), so H100 sits at the 5090's posture against Lium's anchor instead (idle ~55% of it, leased ~1.6x); target fleets are starting sizes, not forecasts. RTX3090 / RTX4090 (10/8): proposals at the same posture (leased near the market midpoint less margin, idle 35% of leased; Lium 4090 ~0.35-0.45, Vast 3090 ~0.20-0.30); both types are listed, not qualified, so no box of either is admitted or paid until a real card is run and Kimbo sets the rows. AMD rows (10/8, vault 30 §8, §14; 31 §7 #1-#2): proposals at the same posture, leased from the 10/8 on-demand midpoints (MI300X: DigitalOcean $1.99, Hot Aisle ~$2.00, TensorWave $1.71 sale; the row sits above the market because idle pay, not the lease, is the operator's draw per 31 §7 #2), idle 35% of leased, target_fleet in multiples of the 8x box the market sells. Every AMD type is listed, not qualified, so no AMD box is admitted or paid until the MI300X run (31 step 1) and Kimbo sets the rows; and a row with no accrued card costs the pool nothing (31 §7 #1 says what the first 8x box does to afford).
_future: Dynamic target fleets (design intention, 2026-10-05, Alex): target_fleet per type should follow demand once the rental product exists. Start from these defaults; when one type is rented a lot and another not at all, move target slots from the idle type to the busy one (e.g. RTX5090 10 -> 12, RTXPRO6000 5 -> 4), clamped to at least 1 of every type, on a slow cadence (daily or weekly). Over-supplied types dilute among themselves as today; the targets move, the rule for a card's pay does not. Not built: it waits for the rental seam (gittensor-app) to produce the demand signal.
